Adding cos/sin terms times x and v, and x²·cos/sin terms, reduced the linear-fit residual to about 1e-3, but the best frequency kept drifting, so the time dependence is still not right. Velocity nonlinearities (|v|, v|v|, sign v) and polynomial-in-t terms did not help.

import numpy as np
def equation(t, x, v, params):
    w=params[0]
    C=np.cos(w*t); S=np.sin(w*t)
    return (params[1] + params[2]*x + params[3]*v + params[4]*x*x + params[5]*x*v
            + params[6]*C + params[7]*S + params[8]*x*C + params[9]*x*S)
